sections.h2: Who sends the Jackson County tax bill
sections.html:
In Jackson County the Tax Collector produces your bill, and the office's online portal lets you look up a parcel by tax year. What the property is worth is the Property Appraiser's call. Tax rates are voted on by the County Commission, the School Board and the other districts that levy against you.

The collector's calendar runs month by month through the year. Vehicle and license deadlines share it with property tax, so the table below picks out only the property rows. Compare them with your contract date to see which deadline comes next.

The county runs on Central Time. If you pay online at the end of a month, check the local clock first.

sections.h2: What are the Jackson County property tax months?
sections.html:
Collection opens in November and ends at the gross amount on March 31, with the discount shrinking in between.

Property tax months for Jackson County
MonthWhat to expect
NovemberCollection opens; 4% discount if paid by November 30
December3% discount
January2% discount
February1% discount
MarchGross amount due by March 31
AprilUnpaid real property tax delinquent on April 1; 3% penalty

Business equipment, which is tangible personal property, follows the same discount months. A homeowner can usually ignore that row, but a landlord or a seller who ran a business from the property should read it.

A 3% penalty lands on real property tax that is still owed on April 1. Within 45 days the delinquent list is printed in a local paper at the owner's cost, then repeated weekly for three weeks in May ahead of the certificate sale. March is when the sale date gets chosen, which lets a seller find out early.

Buying a certificate gives an investor a lien, not the house. When two years pass with no redemption, the investor can ask for a deed and the clerk runs an auction. Where the parcel is a homestead, statute 197.502 adds half of the latest assessed value to the opening bid, in addition to the amount owed.

Equipment taxes run on a different clock: 1.5% interest a month, advertising within 45 days, and tax warrant work from May 1.

sections.h2: Can Jackson County owners spread payments over the year?
sections.html:
Yes. There is a four payment plan against the coming year's tax, and applications are due April 30. Owners already enrolled continue without applying again.

  • First payment: due on or before June 1, with cancellation if nothing arrives by June 30.
  • Second payment: before September 30.
  • Third payment: by December 31.
  • Final payment: by March 31.

Two dates apply to the first payment, so phone the office to learn which governs your account. Selling mid-plan? Give the closing agent your paid installment list so the split is calculated correctly.

Homestead here follows the statewide pattern: occupy the home on January 1, submit DR-501 by March 1, and as much as $50,000 is taken from assessed value. School tax drops only on the first $25,000.

Yearly increases in a homestead's assessed value cannot exceed the smaller of 3 percent or inflation; for 2026 the state chart shows 2.7 percent. Parcels without homestead are limited to a 10 percent increase. Both limits end when the property sells, which is why the buyer's first bill is frequently bigger than the seller's last.

  • Seniors: owners 65 or older with limited income may get an extra exemption if a county or city ordinance provides one.
  • Veteran disability: a disability connected to service, rated 10 percent or more, can earn a $5,000 cut in assessed value.
  • Leasing the house or leaving it removes homestead status.

Check with the Property Appraiser about any local ordinance covering your address.

August brings the TRIM notices, and you have 25 days after that to file a Value Adjustment Board petition. If an exemption is denied, the clock is 30 days from the date of the denial letter.

Start with a conversation at the appraiser's office. Staff can sometimes correct wrong square footage or a wrong exemption status with no hearing at all, and a deed, survey or builder's records back you up when the property record itself is mistaken.

sections.h2: Do mobile homes and business equipment follow the same dates?
sections.html:
Partly. Business furniture and equipment, called tangible personal property, use the same discount schedule as real estate, though a late account pays 1.5% interest each month.

Mobile homes are handled separately. If one is not assessed as real property, its decal must be renewed by December 31, and registrations for mobile homes, trucks over 8,000 pounds and truck-trailers share that December window. Selling land with a mobile home on it? Ask the collector whether the home is billed as real property or carries a decal, because the answer sets your deadline.

Tell the closing agent early whether a mobile home or business equipment goes with the property, so each related account is located and paid before settlement.

A tax balance will not block a sale. It is a lien on the parcel, and the title company handles it as one more payoff. The usual order of events is below.

  1. Request the amount due for every open year from the Tax Collector, noting how long the quote holds.
  2. Pass that figure to the title agent for the settlement statement.
  3. The title agent pays the Tax Collector out of your proceeds at the table, and the lien is released.
  4. File the paid receipt with your closing papers in case an old year surfaces later.

When a certificate has already been sold on the parcel, the payoff must cover what the investor is owed, so ask the office for a redemption figure before choosing a closing date. Buyers paying cash can often close faster here, since nothing waits on a loan approval.

sections.h2: What a seller should line up before closing
sections.html:
Obtain the payoff in writing and note which tax year it covers. At the table, the title agent splits the current year between the two sides.

  • Use the portal's tax-year search to check whether earlier years remain open.
  • If April 1 has already come and gone, ask about the penalty and advertising costs.
  • Search the Clerk's records for recorded liens.
  • Hand the closing agent your installment history.

Put the parcel number, a copy of your deed and your latest bill in one folder, because each office asks for them. Have balances quoted with a date, since totals change during the year. A seller up against a delinquency or certificate sale date can arrange a fast cash closing, with the tax paid from proceeds by the title agent. Without a lender appraisal or underwriting in the way, the schedule depends mostly on the title work.

faqs.q: What is the final day to pay Jackson County property tax without a penalty?
faqs.a: The gross amount is accepted through March 31. Early payment earns 4% in November, then 3%, 2% and 1% over the next three months.

faqs.q: What penalty hits an unpaid Jackson County bill on April 1?
faqs.a: Real property gets a 3% penalty, while business equipment is charged 1.5% interest per month.

faqs.q: When does Jackson County hold its tax certificate sale?
faqs.a: The collector sets the date in March, before April 1 delinquency begins. Call the collector for the exact day.

faqs.q: Does Jackson County allow installment payments?
faqs.a: Yes. Apply by April 30 for the following year, then pay in June, September, December and March. The office can confirm the June date.

faqs.q: Will selling raise the next owner's Jackson County bill?
faqs.a: Usually. A sale ends the Save Our Homes cap and the 10 percent limit, and the following January 1 resets the property to just value.
